lessons.statement: wrap1_zhyp logger's every-10-step bucket_grad_l2 used a second SDRP backward on train_batches[0] while Adam averaged 11 structures. Projector sawtooth was primarily that measurement mismatch. Next harness card must log grads from the train backward itself.

lessons.title: This line's recent findings are measurement corrections, not architecture verdicts
lessons.statement: Pooled AUPRC, dehydron-off-spine, unreachable lift bars, mean-only F1, and 3-not-5 effective SDRP classes were instrument/scope failures. SDRP-live spine reach is confirmed wiring. lessons.process_gap: treat INCONCLUSIVE_UNDERFIT or low moe grad as architecture incapacity before instruments are trustworthy

lessons.title: SE(3)-lite frontend findings cover a 1-block stub, not frontend architecture capacity
lessons.statement: StubEquiformerFrontend._se3_lite_forward (science/tokyo_eye/v8/equiformer_frontend.py) only ever executes self.backbone.blocks[0]; 84 of 91 backbone-block parameters (6 of the nominal 7 blocks) are structurally outside the loss graph regardless of LR, steps, or coefficient tuning. Every prior SE(3)-lite finding describing the frontend as 'barely moved' (z_hyp G_fit, M2 capacity) was correctly measured but scoped to 1-block-stub capacity, not frontend architecture capacity -- do not cite those numbers as evidence about frontend capacity in general. Swapping in the real EquiformerV3 pool frontend (cold_init, no MPtrj ckpt) reaches gradient in 288/292 frontend tensors (only the unused OC20 energy head stays NONE) on the same diagnostic scale. Spine/wiring conclusions from those cards are unaffected -- this is a scope correction on the frontend side only, not a retraction.
lessons.process_gap: reading 'frontend barely moved under SE(3)-lite' as evidence about frontend architecture capacity, rather than checking whether the lite stub's forward actually executes all nominal blocks

lessons.title: A script's result being recorded durably does not make the script itself reproducible
lessons.statement: Twice in one session, a script was written to /tmp on the reasoning that only its *output* needed to survive (a diagnostic finding, a benchmark number already quoted in a prereg). Both times this was wrong: if the script itself doesn't exist anywhere durable, nobody -- including a future instance of this agent -- can re-run it to verify the claim, reproduce it on different hardware, or extend it. First instance (gradient-flow diagnostics, checkpoint/pure_hyp verification) was caught by the operator and fixed by moving to scripts/diag_gradflow_pool_frontend.py with pinned deps. Second instance (scripts/bench_pool_frontend_step_time.py, used to size the M2 pool-LR prereg's compute budget) was caught by the operator asking directly why /tmp was being used again, after the first fix. Rule going forward: if a script's number is going to be quoted in a gate, card, or prereg, the script itself is part of the evidence and belongs in scripts/, not /tmp -- there is no such thing as a disposable-script/durable-result split.
lessons.process_gap: treating a script as disposable scratch work because its output, not the script itself, seemed like the thing that needed to persist

items.title: Equiformer-pool frontend capacity or biology (separate sealed card)
items.note: Lite result is not pool evidence. Capacity on pool still needs reachable bars. Diagnostic 2026-09-22 (scripts/diag_gradflow_pool_frontend.py; non-claim, do_not_promote, off-path -- cold_init pool frontend, no MPtrj ckpt, activation-checkpointed backbone, 4/12 train structures for GPU-memory reasons): gradient reaches 288/292 frontend tensors (vs 25/117 under SE(3)-lite -- see L-se3-lite-frontend-1-of-7-blocks). At lr_frontend=1e-5 (sealed value) train fit on those 4 structures reproduces the M2 card's stuck floor almost exactly (min_f1 0.327/0.324 vs sealed min ~0.31-0.33). At lr_frontend=1e-4, same 4 structures clear decisively -- train macro_f1 0.895, min_f1 0.865 -- with per-structure lift>1 and macro_f1 well above majority-basin on every structure, including the one pinned at exact majority under 1e-5 (1TEN:A: acc=maj=0.933/lift=1.000/f1=0.32 -> acc=0.989/lift=1.060/f1=0.887), which rules out majority-sharpening as the explanation. TRAIN-FIT ONLY, NOT HELD-OUT: 4 of 12 structures (76-155 residues), 200 of 400 steps. Those 4 are exactly 3 of the 4 lowest-held-out-F1 folds in the sealed 12-fold M2 result (1UBQ 0.307, 1TEN 0.316, 1LYZ 0.317 -- the 3 lowest of 12; 1HHP 0.320 mid-pack), i.e. historically hard-to-generalize structures, not easy ones -- but this diagnostic still says nothing about held-out performance at this LR/frontend combination. Process checks passed clean for this exact config: gradient-checkpointing bit-equivalence (max abs grad diff 4.5e-8 over 318 tensors) and pure_hyp_pass (0 violations). Execution started 2026-09-22 18:13 UTC: lr_1e-4 arm, full 400 steps, all 12 folds (operator 'go' on the agent's recommended scope; prereg data/gates/tokyo_eye_equ_wrap1_zhyp_m2_pool_lr_prereg.json flipped DRAFT->READY_TO_RUN for this arm only). Benchmarked at 31.5s/step, ~42h expected wall-clock, single 4GB GPU. sealed (1e-5) control arm on the same pool frontend is a planned follow-up once this arm's result lands, NOT skipped -- without it, 'the LR change specifically mattered' stays an inference from the earlier 4-structure diagnostic, not this sealed run's own isolation. Do not read or report on individual fold results before all 12 land.
items.next: sealed prereg when bars/target ready Directionally-promising diagnostic (2026-09-22) supports drafting that prereg sooner rather than later: isolate frontend LR alone (pool@1e-5 vs pool@1e-4, frontend architecture held fixed), full 12-structure LOSO, scored against the already-locked M2 mean+min macro-F1 bar -- do not combine the LR change with any other simultaneous change (e.g. euc_skip removal).
